prompt: A single RimWorld creature sprite in a loose, painterly, realistic vanilla RimWorld style, on a transparent background, with a clean, thin, soft, dark outline of even weight all the way around the body that stays readable at normal game scale. The gawpsack is a drifting, soft, sagging sack floating in open air at treetop height, with no water, no dome and no limbs. Its body is one continuous, thin, pale, semi-translucent membrane, narrower and slumped at the top, heavy and bulging lower down, lumpy and uneven like an overstuffed bag. The skin is a thin translucent membrane with the eyes pressed against it from inside, dimly visible through it on every facing. One continuous outer membrane visibly encloses the whole cluster of tightly packed eyes, stretching over them like cling film over a bag of marbles. The eyes overlap one another, their contours crowding and pressing together. Their muted iris colours show through the soft folds and creases of the skin. Between and over the eyes the membrane is smooth, pale and slightly cloudy, with no separate sockets or rims. Fine pale veins cross the membrane. The membrane bulges gently outward over each eyeball. On the rear view, seen from behind, the back of the bag shows faint rounded eye shapes and pale muted irises beneath the skin across its bulges, so the packed eyes read as contents of the bag from every side. The eyes differ in shape, size and colour: round eyes, slit-pupilled goat-like eyes, elongated eyes including a few gold ones, and a few with several pupils, in varied iris colours. The eyeballs are not uniform spheres: some are squashed, oval or lumpy where they press against their neighbours. Every eye, including the elongated gold ones, has its upper and lower lids parted wide, with a broad band of white sclera visible around the iris, so each eye reads as fully open. Every iris and pupil is rolled clearly to the top of the eyeball, gazing up toward the sky, with a crescent of pale lower sclera showing beneath each iris. The flesh and eyes are painted with looser visible brushwork and matte, softly worn surfaces, like vanilla RimWorld creatures. Shading uses broad painterly value masses, a lighter upper body and a darker heavier lower body, with only a few small, soft, deliberately placed highlights and hand-painted texture.
